key_facts: The team decided to drop the speech recognition feature.
The team agreed to keep the LCD screen and the advanced chip-on-print display.
The team opted for a single curved design with a flat side.
The team decided to replace most buttons with an integrated scroll-wheel push-button.
The team identified the need for a power button and a menu button.
The team concluded that the remote control should have a special color for the button and frame.
The team discussed the cost implications and determined that the integrated scroll-wheel push-button would cost more than individual buttons.
The team decided to use a hand dynamo as a power source.
The team evaluated the remote control on a seven-point scale and scored it a 2 for matching the operating behavior of the young user.
The team scored the remote control a 5 for showing relevant and most used functions.
The team scored the remote control a 2 for being easy to use.
The team scored the remote control a 2 for displaying the corporate logo.
The team scored the remote control a 4 for being a good example of the company's motto of putting fashion in electronics.
The team calculated an overall score of approximately 3.11 by dividing the sum of scores by 9.
The team decided to use a special color for the remote control, with red being suggested as an option.
The team planned to create a logo for the remote control, referencing the initials R and another R.
The team mentioned the need for recalibrating the drawing tool due to projection issues.
The team concluded the meeting with plans to finalize the report and prepare for a presentation.
